claims.claim_text: Bell's major U.S. Government programs are the V-22 tiltrotor aircraft and the H-1 helicopter platforms, both in the production and support stage, and they represent a significant portion of Bell's revenues from the U.S. Government.
claims.subject: Bell (Textron segment)
claims.object_value: V-22 tiltrotor + H-1 helicopter program-of-record revenue
claims.source_quote: Bell's major U.S. Government programs at this time are the V-22 tiltrotor aircraft and the H-1 helicopter platforms, which are both in the production and support stage and represent a significant portion of Bell's revenues from the U.S. Government.

claims.claim_text: Over the next several years, the H-1 helicopter program with the U.S. Government will be transitioning from the production stage to the support stage.
claims.subject: Bell H-1 program (USMC AH-1Z / UH-1Y)
claims.source_quote: Over the next several years, the H-1 helicopter program with the U.S. Government will be transitioning from the production stage to the support stage.

claims.claim_text: Bell's operating expenses included higher research and development costs, largely related to the Future Vertical Lift programs (FLRAA / FARA), and Bell's military revenues declined in 2021 reflecting the winddown of the H-1 production program.
claims.subject: Bell Future Vertical Lift exposure
claims.object_value: FLRAA (V-280 Valor) and FARA next-gen Army rotorcraft pipeline
claims.source_quote: Bell's operating expenses increased $109 million, 4%, in 2021, compared with 2020, primarily due to higher net volume and mix described above and higher research and development costs, largely related to the future vertical lift programs.

claims.claim_text: Textron Systems' revenue concentration includes Shadow tactical UAS and Aerosonde small UAS, with U.S. Army withdrawal from Afghanistan reducing fee-for-service revenues by $79 million in 2021.
claims.subject: Textron Systems Shadow / Aerosonde UAS
claims.object_value: Shadow RQ-7 (FTUAS-to-be-replaced) and Aerosonde fee-for-service contracts
claims.source_quote: Lower volume of $16 million included a $79 million decrease from our fee-for-service contracts, primarily reflecting the impact from the U.S. Army's withdrawal from Afghanistan, partially offset by higher volume at ATAC of $69 million... [Textron Systems product lines include] Shadow [and] Aerosonde

claims.claim_text: Approximately 26% of Textron's 2021 revenues were derived from contracts with the U.S. Government, including those under the U.S. Government-sponsored foreign military sales program.
claims.subject: Textron consolidated DoD/FMS exposure
claims.object_value: 26% of 2021 revenues from U.S. Government contracts
claims.source_quote: Approximately 26% of our 2021 revenues were derived from contracts with the U.S. Government, including those under the U.S. Government-sponsored foreign military sales program.

claims.claim_text: Textron Aviation's military trainer and defense aircraft franchise includes the T-6 trainer (used by 20+ countries) and the AT-6 light attack military aircraft, which represent forward DoD trainer pipeline exposure.
claims.subject: Textron Aviation T-6 / AT-6
claims.object_value: T-6 Texan II trainer + AT-6 light attack pipeline
claims.source_quote: Textron Aviation's military trainer and defense aircraft include the T-6 trainer, which has been used to train pilots from more than 20 countries, and the AT-6 light attack military aircraft.

claims.claim_text: Bell's backlog decreased $1.5 billion, 28%, in 2021, primarily as a result of revenues recognized on U.S. Government contracts in excess of new contracts received — indicating shrinking forward DoD pipeline at Bell prior to FY2022 J-Book.
claims.subject: Bell backlog trajectory
claims.source_quote: Bell's backlog decreased $1.5 billion, 28%, in 2021, primarily as a result of revenues recognized on our U.S. Government contracts in excess of new contracts received.

claims.claim_text: Textron Systems' backlog decreased $412 million in 2021 to $2.144B, primarily due to revenues recognized in excess of new contracts received.
claims.subject: Textron Systems backlog
claims.source_quote: Backlog at Textron Systems decreased $412 million in 2021, primarily due to revenues recognized in excess of new contracts received.

claims.claim_text: [CONTROL] Approximately 29% of Textron's $2.5 billion 2022 purchase obligations represent purchase orders issued for goods and services to be delivered under firm contracts with the U.S. Government.
claims.subject: Textron purchase obligations
claims.object_value: ~$725M of $2.5B 2022 purchase obligations tied to firm US Gov contracts
claims.source_quote: Approximately 29% of our purchase obligations represent purchase orders issued for goods and services to be delivered under firm contracts with the U.S. Government for which we have full recourse under customary contract termination clauses.

claims.claim_text: [CONTROL] Textron operated 52 plants in the U.S. and 45 plants outside the U.S. (97 total, 58 owned) totaling approximately 23.3 million square feet of manufacturing space as of January 1, 2022.
claims.subject: Textron manufacturing footprint
claims.source_quote: On January 1, 2022, we operated a total of 52 plants located throughout the U.S. and 45 plants outside the U.S. We own 58 plants and lease the remainder for a total manufacturing space of approximately 23.3 million square feet.
